nodes.label: One Crafted Token per Exception Type
nodes.norm_label: one crafted token per exception type
nodes.rationale: isTokenValid has four catch blocks; each is triggered by a purpose-built token (malformed, negative lifetime, alg:none, empty) rather than by stubbing the parser, so the test exercises real JJWT behaviour.

nodes.label: Invalid Base64 Test JWT Secret
nodes.rationale: The literal string 'test' is not a valid Base64 256-bit key, so Keys.hmacShaKeyFor threw WeakKeyException on any signing operation. Fixing it was the prerequisite for every token test.

nodes.label: erd.app.jwt Properties
nodes.rationale: Secret, access/refresh expirations and both cookie names live under one namespace, read via @Value in JwtService; the compose file overrides exactly these keys from .env.

nodes.label: Base64 Test JWT Secret
nodes.rationale: A 61-byte Base64 secret because JJWT's Keys.hmacShaKeyFor requires >= 256 bits for HS256; the previous literal 'test' made every signing operation throw WeakKeyException.

nodes.label: Two Unreachable Branches Removed
nodes.rationale: Pursuing 100% branch coverage proved two DdlService conditions invariant - a regex group that always matches and a containsKey guard over a map built from the same regex - and they were deleted. The only production change made by the coverage work.

nodes.label: Cookie-Based Auth Contract for the Client
nodes.norm_label: cookie-based auth contract for the client
nodes.rationale: The API sets erd-token and erd-refresh-token as HttpOnly cookies, so every frontend request needs withCredentials:true and there is no Authorization header to stub; a browser 401 means the cookie was not sent, not that CORS blocked it.

nodes.label: doAnswer for Undeclared Checked Exceptions
nodes.rationale: The catch(Exception) arm sits after catch(RuntimeException), so it is only reachable via a checked exception; Mockito's thenThrow refuses one the method does not declare, but an Answer lambda declares throws Throwable and does.

nodes.label: No Global Exception Handler
nodes.rationale: Only TokenControllerAdvice exists; every other controller wraps its body in try/catch and returns badRequest/notFound/internalServerError inline, which is the single largest source of branches in the controller layer.

nodes.label: Authentication and Token Refresh Flow
nodes.rationale: findOrCreate has three distinct outcomes - no token, expired-and-rotated, and valid-and-reused - which is why it needs three separate tests.

nodes.label: Bare RuntimeException Error Signalling
nodes.rationale: Business errors are raised as new RuntimeException(...) throughout the service layer, so callers cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'forbidden' except by message text.

nodes.label: Request Authorization Flow
nodes.rationale: JwtAuthenticationFilter swallows every exception by design: an invalid token yields an anonymous request rather than a 500, so failure surfaces as 401/403 rather than a server error.

nodes.label: Real-Time Diagram Editing
nodes.rationale: Mutations travel over STOMP/WebSocket, are persisted, then re-broadcast to every other client on the project topic.

nodes.label: WebSocket Handshake Authentication
nodes.rationale: The JWT cookie is copied into the WebSocket session attributes during the HTTP handshake, then turned into an Authentication on STOMP CONNECT - the socket cannot read cookies later, so the copy must happen at handshake time.

nodes.label: Guards and Interceptor Parity
nodes.rationale: Testing a component method directly bypasses the route guard exactly as standalone MockMvc bypasses @PreAuthorize, so guards and the JWT interceptor need their own specs.

nodes.label: Hybrid Controller Testing
nodes.rationale: Standalone MockMvc drives all three outcomes of every endpoint fast, but it ignores @PreAuthorize - so @WebMvcTest slices with spring-security-test are added to prove the authorization rules actually reject unauthorized callers.

nodes.label: GitHub Container Registry Target
nodes.rationale: Images are tagged both :latest and :<sha> and pushed to GHCR on every push to main, with GitHub Actions layer caching to keep the Maven build affordable.

nodes.label: CI Coverage Enforcement
nodes.rationale: `mvn -B verify` is used rather than `test` precisely because verify is the phase the JaCoCo check rule binds to, so a coverage regression fails the pull request instead of merely reporting a lower number.

nodes.label: JaCoCo Report Artifact Upload
nodes.rationale: Uploaded with `if: always()` so the HTML report is still retrievable from a red build - the report is what explains why the gate failed.

nodes.label: SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON Override
nodes.rationale: Runtime configuration is injected as one JSON blob so the container reuses the packaged application.yml while pointing datasource, Mongo URI and JWT settings at compose service names and .env secrets.

nodes.label: erd-client Angular Frontend
nodes.rationale: The Angular counterpart of erd-core; the playbook exists to repeat the backend coverage result there, starting from 39 source files, 8 stub specs and 0 executed tests.

nodes.label: Istanbul via karma-coverage
nodes.rationale: The frontend analogue of JaCoCo; needs lcovonly emitted for SonarQube and a check.global threshold block for the gate.

nodes.label: Phased Migration Plan
nodes.rationale: Repair the suite first, write tests, then turn on the threshold - otherwise every intermediate commit is red and git bisect becomes useless.

nodes.label: Templates Are Not Instrumented
nodes.rationale: Istanbul covers .ts only, so branches inside *ngIf/*ngFor and pipes never appear; 100% must be stated as not covering template logic.

nodes.label: TypeScript Interface Erasure
nodes.rationale: All ten model files declare interface, not class. TypeScript erases interfaces at compile time so they emit no JavaScript - Istanbul never sees them, meaning the backend's 700-line DTO problem simply does not exist here.

nodes.label: Untested Files Are Absent, Not 0%
nodes.rationale: src/test.ts uses require.context over spec files, so webpack only bundles - and Istanbul only instruments - files reachable from a spec. A service nobody tests vanishes from the denominator entirely, making '100% over 8 of 39 files' meaningless.

nodes.label: Diagram Broadcast Goes to /topic/diagram/null
nodes.rationale: WebSocketService builds the destination from savedDto.getProjectId(), but DiagramMapper.toResponseDto never populates projectId. Recorded, deliberately not fixed, so the coverage work stayed purely additive.

nodes.label: Collaborative ERD Editor
nodes.rationale: The whole architecture follows from one requirement: several users edit the same diagram at once, so the backend must hold the canonical diagram, broadcast every mutation and arbitrate concurrent edits.

nodes.label: Dead application-test.yml Profile
nodes.rationale: No test activates the 'test' profile, so the file never loads; its Mongo settings were copied into the application.yml that is loaded.

nodes.label: Entity Locking
nodes.rationale: Locks are held in an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap rather than the database because they are session-scoped: they expire on a schedule and are dropped wholesale when the holder's WebSocket session disconnects.

nodes.label: JaCoCo BUNDLE Coverage Gate
nodes.rationale: A LINE/BRANCH/METHOD/CLASS COVEREDRATIO >= 1.00 rule bound to verify, because a coverage figure nobody enforces decays; the gate was added last so intermediate commits stayed green and bisectable.

nodes.label: mockStatic for Static Entry Points
nodes.rationale: Used twice: to reach the failure branch guarding SecurityContextHolder access, and to execute CoreApplication.main without booting a second application context.

nodes.label: No Coverage Exclusions
nodes.rationale: Excluding DTOs, entities and config would remove roughly a third of the codebase from the denominator, so a '100%' claim would describe a filtered subset rather than the system. The JaCoCo rule is applied at BUNDLE level over everything under src/main/java.

nodes.label: No Lombok, No Records
nodes.rationale: Hand-written accessors mean ~700 lines of the codebase are getters/setters that still count as coverable code - this single absence is what forces the reflective POJO harness.

nodes.label: Reflective POJO Contract Testing
nodes.rationale: One parameterized test replaces 30 near-identical POJO test classes while still executing every constructor and accessor, including read-only DTOs whose fields Jackson populates directly in production.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Full Stack
nodes.rationale: Recommended local setup: one compose file orchestrates PostgreSQL, MongoDB, backend and frontend so the whole system runs with a single command; a cached Maven volume keeps rebuilds fast.

nodes.label: Local Development Without Docker
nodes.rationale: Java 17/Maven path documented as an alternative; only the databases are containerised via docker-compose-local.yml while the application runs on the host for faster iteration.

nodes.label: H2 In-Memory Test Datasource
nodes.rationale: Swapping PostgreSQL for H2 lets the @SpringBootTest context - the one that covers the config package for free - boot without any database running.

nodes.label: Unused test Profile Mongo Config
nodes.rationale: Never loaded because no test activates the test profile; its settings were copied into src/test/resources/application.yml, which is loaded. Kept in place but identified as deletable.
